answer: Reputation-weighted transaction tax. Each new identity starts at a low trust score, so every transaction it initiates pays a tax that declines as verified counterparties independently confirm real activity. An attacker's clone network hits a cost zenith fast because mutual confirmations between its own sybes earn near-zero reputation weight, leaving each fake identity paying the full tax rate on every trade. A genuine operator's reputation plume grows through diverse external partners, while fake clusters stay in a low-trust velvet trap where volume multiplies cost instead of amortizing it.
